To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MyoD1 induces transdifferentiation of human epidermal keratinocytes to the mesenchymal/ myogenic phenotype, but not to the epidermal lineage.

MyoD1 is able to induce a myogenic program in human keratinocytes, but that the epidermal and myogenic programs are independently controlled, and that a subpopulation of less adherent cells isolated from 5-azaCdR-treated MyoD1- transfected HaCaT cells can transdifferentiate to the myogenic phenotype.
MyoD1 is able to transactivate myogenic genes in human keratinocytes and that this transactivation can be enhanced by 5-aza-dC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the epigenetic control of cell fate and the mechanisms of cell type conversion.
the question of how a cell can be induced to change its phenotype, and the answer may be that it requires more than a single step.
the epigenetic regulation of epidermal and mesenchymal differentiation and the molecular mechanisms involved.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MyoD1 can induce a mesenchymally directed "transdifferentiation", but the epidermal keratinocyte phenotype is stable.

the MyoD1 gene, when transfected into human epidermal keratinocytes, induces a "transdifferentiation process" which is characterized by a progressive change from an epidermal to a mesenchyme/myogenic phenotype.
the MyoD1 gene, when introduced in a fully differentiated epidermal cell, can induce a "transdifferentiation", i.e., a change from one differentiated phenotype to another.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MyoD1 can induce a transdifferentiation process in human epidermal keratinocytes, but the epidermal and mesenchymal phenotypes are not readily converted into each other.
the MyoD1 gene can convert human epidermal keratinocytes to a myogenic pathway without affecting the epidermal cell phenotype.

MyoD1 is able to induce the synthesis of myogenic markers without altering the epidermis-specific gene expression, that 5-azaC treatment of MyoD-transfected keratinocytes results in an epithelial cell type that has lost its capacity to form a stratified epithelium in transplants, and that a subpopulation of these cells has acquired a mesenchymale/myogenic phenotype.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MyoD1 gene is able to induce a transdifferentiation process in human keratinocytes.
MyoD1 can induce transdifferentiation of epidermal cells to a mesenchyml/myogenic phenotype.
the keratinocyte lineage can be converted to the myogenic lineage by transfection with MyoD1 and that this conversion can occur without loss of keratinocyte characteristics.
